name: Ligenza
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

sources.citation: Motingea Mangulu, André. 2002. Le parler des Bendza d'Aketi, dialecte ngombe de la Province Orientale. Annales Aequatoria 23: 329-404.
sources.access_detail: a digital copy (available on request); access check: a digital copy exists, behind a library sign-in
sources.note: Section 2 'Phonétique et phonologie' (pp. 336-349) covers vowels (length non-phonemic, p. 336), consonants, semivowels, tones (2.4, p. 349: two level tones H/L plus rising and falling contours, with minimal pairs) and syllables (2.5, p. 349: open syllables V, CV, CSV). No mention of stress, accent, intensity or penultimate prominence anywhere in the article.

sources.citation: Motingea Mangulu, André. 1995. Note sur le parler des Babale de la Dua. Annales Aequatoria 16: 365-401.
sources.access_detail: a digital copy (available on request); access check: a digital copy exists, behind a library sign-in
sources.note: Section II 'Sons' (pp. 367-374): 2.3 Tons (p. 373) 'Il existe deux tons de base : bas et haut' with contour tones from elision/fusion and lexical/grammatical minimal pairs; 2.4 Syllabation (p. 374) open syllables. Nothing on stress/accent. Note the variety is 'ibale' of the Babale of the Dua, which the author calls a Ngombe-Doko mixture; Glottolog files it under lige1238 but it is not Genza proper.

sources.citation: Motingea Mangulu, André. 1993. Les langues Mabinja (Uele) et Ngombe (C.41). Annales Aequatoria 14: 503-516.
sources.note: Entry-by-entry commentary on Hedborg's (1910) Mabinza vocabulary compared with Ngombe (Rood 1958); geo-historical framing only, no phonology, nothing on tone or stress.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.1 languoid page lige1238; Wikipedia 'Gendza language' stub
sources.note: Nothing on phonology; Glottolog names Motingea 2001 pp. 101-102 for subclassification only.

sources.note: The sketch of Genja/Ligenza proper (Genja of Bolupi, Bumba-Lisala), the variety Glottolog's lige1238 actually denotes; Motingea's sketches carry a 'Tons' section and this one would supersede the Bendza-of-Aketi data. Whether it says anything about stress is unknown.
